title: Coarse-grained kinetic scale tightens thermodynamic spectral bounds of Markov cycles
abstract: Thermodynamic bounds on the spectrum of a Markov cycle depend on the cycle affinity and maximum escape rate, but they ignore how the local transition rates are distributed around the cycle. In this work, we show that a single additional cycle-wide kinetic quantity, the geometric means of forward and backward rates, yields a strictly stronger bound for every nonuniform cycle. By comparing each winding sector of the eigenmode with a product-matched uniform cycle, we bound oscillation frequencies, tighten the admissible spectral region, and show that only uniform cycles can saturate the Uhl-Seifert boundary. Our results show that retaining a coarse-grained kinetic scale can sharpen thermodynamic spectral bounds without requiring knowledge of the full generator. Our method also provides a complex-analytic framework which unifies generator-specific kinetic information with established affinity-winding bounds.
summary: This paper refines the spectral bounds for Markov cycles by incorporating a coarse-grained kinetic scale derived from the geometric means of forward and backward transition rates. Using complex analysis and Floquet theory, the authors prove that this new kinetic information yields a strictly tighter bound than previously known universal bounds. This advances the understanding of how local rate distributions constrain the long-time dynamics of open quantum systems.
main_problem: To sharpen the thermodynamic spectral bounds for Markov cycles beyond those depending only on cycle affinity and maximum escape rate.
main_result: The authors derive a strictly stronger spectral bound using a single additional kinetic quantity—the geometric means of forward and backward rates—which is only saturated by uniform cycles.
method: The analysis employs complex-analytic techniques, transforming the eigenvalue problem into a reciprocal Jacobi form and utilizing Floquet theory to derive refined spectral constraints.
model_or_system: The system is a continuous-time Markov jump process on a ring of $n$ states, governed by a master equation whose generator $R$ defines the dynamics.
key_observables: Eigenvalues $\lambda$ (specifically $	ext{Im } \lambda > 0$), oscillation frequencies, and the spectral region defined by the bounds.
important_parameters: Cycle affinity ($A$), geometric means of rates ($G^+, G^-$), and the dimensionless kinetic scale ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on genuinely oscillatory modes and assumes the existence of a coarse-grained kinetic scale that can be incorporated into the bounds.
figures_summary: Figures compare the original nonuniform cycle rates to the product-matched uniform cycle rates, illustrating how the new kinetic factor $\kappa$ localizes and sharpens the spectral bounds compared to the universal affinity-winding bounds.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the limitations of existing bounds to introducing the geometric mean kinetic scale, deriving the refined spectral bound via complex-analytic methods (Floquet theory/Jacobi forms), and finally demonstrating the strict improvement over previous universal bounds.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general framework for refining spectral bounds in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics by incorporating local kinetic details into global thermodynamic constraints, which is highly relevant for open quantum systems.
